clinician.final_diagnosis: PIMS-TS (Paediatric Inflammatory Multisystem Syndrome Temporally associated with SARS-CoV-2)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A school-aged boy presented with a 2-day history of fever, central/lower abdominal pain, reduced appetite, and vomiting. Initial suspicion was acute appendicitis, but an ultrasound showed inflammatory changes between the stomach and pancreas, and serum amylase was normal. Initial blood tests revealed elevated C-reactive protein (130 mg/L) and D-dimer (1126 ng/mL). Subsequent investigations showed positive SARS-CoV-2 IgG and IgM antibodies, while COVID-19 PCR was negative. An echocardiogram identified borderline low left ventricular function, mild mitral regurgitation, and a small pericardial effusion. The diagnosis of PIMS-TS was concluded based on the clinical picture, positive COVID-19 antibodies, echocardiography findings, inflammatory markers (CRP up to 274 mg/L and raised D-dimer), and response to steroids, in the absence of another cause.
